2609.00858.title: Verifiable Disaster Storylines and Causal Knowledge Graphs: A Citation-Grounded Pipeline from Heterogeneous Humanitarian Sources
2609.00858.paper_summary: Effective humanitarian response depends on the rapid synthesis of heterogeneous, high-volume information sources - a task that routinely exceeds human analytical capacity in the critical early hours of a crisis. We present a pipeline that combines structured disaster records from EM-DAT with unstructured documents from ReliefWeb and the European Media Monitor (EMM) to produce source-grounded disaster storylines and causal knowledge graphs supporting situational awareness for responders and analysts. Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation, the pipeline extracts structured storylines - tabular event profiles covering 17 fields, from severity and key drivers to child-sensitive impact indicators - and constructs causal knowledge graphs where each node and edge is enriched with citation-grounded explanatory narratives, enabling full traceability back to primary sources. We evaluate the system on three diverse crisis use cases through a human evaluation involving 9 domain expert and 9 non-expert evaluators. Results confirm high retrieval precision, strong faithfulness of extracted causal relations, and a clear expert preference for citation-grounded components over ungrounded alternatives. The pipeline is designed to scale to the full EM-DAT catalogue, with the goal of publicly releasing a narrative-enriched version of the database.
2609.00858.paper_summary_zh: 有效的人道主義反應依賴於快速綜合異質的高容量信息來源——這一任務在危機的關鍵早期階段常常超出人類的分析能力。我們提出了一個管道，將來自 EM-DAT 的結構化災難記錄與來自 ReliefWeb 和歐洲媒體監測（EMM）的非結構化文件相結合，以生成基於來源的災難故事情節和因果知識圖，支持應對者和分析師的情境意識。通過檢索增強生成，該管道提取結構化故事情節——涵蓋 17 個領域的表格事件概況，從嚴重性和關鍵驅動因素到兒童敏感影響指標——並構建因果知識圖，其中每個節點和邊緣都附有基於引用的解釋性敘述，實現對主要來源的完整可追溯性。我們通過涉及 9 位領域專家和 9 位非專家評估者的人類評估，對該系統在三個不同的危機使用案例上進行評估。結果確認了高檢索精度、提取的因果關係的強忠實性，以及專家對基於引用的組件相較於無根據替代品的明顯偏好。該管道旨在擴展到完整的 EM-DAT 目錄，目標是公開釋放一個敘述豐富的數據庫版本。
